finding.claim: The ban endpoint swallows the admin check failure via a broad except Exception, so do_ban runs for non-admin users (authorization bypass).
finding.source: uid path parameter in POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban (admin.py:14-15), reached by any request where g.user is a non-admin user dict.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a state-changing protected operation (stub in this repo).

trace.note: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban routes to ban(uid); no login or role decorator
except Exception catches HTTPException (subclass of Exception), swallowing the 403

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only check and is neutralized by except Exception at line 18; no login_required/role decorator/before_request hook in repo; no CSRF or rate limiting visible; unban (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin without try and correctly returns 403. g.user is set outside this repo, so the non-admin precondition depends on external auth middleware (not reviewed). If g.user is None, line 19 raises AttributeError -> 500, no ban (crash, not bypass).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is the only check. It aborts with 403, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try and the bare except Exception at admin.py:18 swallows the HTTPException, so do_ban at admin.py:20 still runs. No login, role decorator, or before_request hook exists in the repo (admin.py is the only file). Unban (admin.py:26) calls require_admin without try, so it correctly blocks.
verdict.reason: The ban handler at admin.py:17-20 wraps require_admin in a bare except Exception at admin.py:18, which catches Werkzeug's abort(403) HTTPException raised at admin.py:11, so do_ban(uid) runs for any request whose g.user is a non-admin. The only precondition is that g.user is set to a non-admin user, which external auth middleware (not in this repo) would normally provide.

finding.claim: On failed admin check the account name (PII) is written to logs, violating org policy against logging PII.
finding.guards_checked: No redaction, masking, or hashing applied to the logged name. Policy violation, not an exploit path.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only control is require_admin (admin.py:9-11), which calls abort(403) and raises. Its raise is caught by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18 and swallowed, so nothing stops execution. No redaction or hashing is applied to the name logged at admin.py:19.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: require_admin at admin.py:17 raises via abort(403) at admin.py:11, admin.py:18 swallows it, and admin.py:19 logs g.user.get("name") unredacted, so the claimed logging of account name occurs for any non-admin caller of /admin/users/<uid>/ban. The finding is a logging-policy issue as stated, but the same lines show a more serious defect the candidate missed: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 still runs after the swallowed failure, so any authenticated non-admin can ban users.
